translation.literal: “Tat savituḥ”: to the one whose self is Brahmā, to the two thumbs, homage. “Vareṇyam”: to the Viṣṇu-self, to the forefingers, homage. “Bhargo devasya”: to the Rudra-self, to the middle fingers, homage. “Dhīmahi”: to the Īśvara-self, to the ring fingers, homage. “Dhiyo yo naḥ”: to the Sadāśiva-self, to the little fingers, homage. “Pracodayāt”: to the self of all, to the palms and backs of the hands, homage.
translation.readable: The six parts of the Gāyatrī are placed on the hands, each with its deity: tat savituḥ (Brahmā) on the thumbs, vareṇyam (Viṣṇu) on the forefingers, bhargo devasya (Rudra) on the middle fingers, dhīmahi (Īśvara) on the ring fingers, dhiyo yo naḥ (Sadāśiva) on the little fingers, pracodayāt (the Self of all) on the palms and backs of the hands.

units.pause_note: Each line names a part of the Gāyatrī and then its deity; the part is quoted, with a pause after it, so तत्सवितुः keeps its pausal visarga before ब्रह्मात्मने.

meaning: A nyāsa (‘placing’) of the Gāyatrī on the hands before the japa. The mantra is cut into six parts; each part is joined to a deity — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva, and finally the Self of all — and touched to a finger in order, from the thumbs to the little fingers, and last the palms and backs of the hands. The formula is the same in each line: the words of the Gāyatrī, the deity in the dative with -ātmane, the fingers in the dative dual, and namaḥ.
in_the_rite: Step nyāsa, all three services, after the viniyoga of the Gāyatrī japa (vin-savitri), in the Mylapore prayoga only; it is followed by the aṅga-nyāsa.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The pairing of each part of the Gāyatrī with a deity and a finger is as M gives it; S has no nyāsa.

flags.text: Two things keep the proof from closing on the text as it stands: (1) M writes तत्स॑वि॒तुः ब्रह्मात्मने with the visarga unjoined before b (proposed: तत्स॑वि॒तुर्ब्रह्मात्मने); (2) the text carries svara marks on the Gāyatrī words, and the sandhi engine compares accented letters — the check should strip accents from the lines of a rite text before the word-division proof. With both, the padaccheda rejoins (declared pauses: ब्रह्मात्मने·अङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम्, धीमहि·ईश्वरात्मने, ईश्वरात्मने·अनामिकाभ्याम्).
